$comment: Derived from the changelog's released sections by the changelog skill (consumer-actions-record.ts); the release step rewrites it, so never edit it by hand.

actions.description: **Breaking:** the copy holds tracked files only. A `ci.log_command` that relied on something installed or generated in the working tree (`node_modules`, build output) no longer finds it, and the copy is not a git checkout, so `git` and `gh` do not find the repository from its working directory.
actions.instruction: Make the command self-contained, or have it install what it needs and give `gh` `-R <owner>/<repo>`; a script that imports only Bun's built-ins and files in the repository needs nothing.

actions.description: `tracker.ts` exits with one code per class: `5` for a spent rate limit, as before, with its `RATE-LIMITED until <time>` line, then `6` unreachable, `7` too costly, `8` server fault, `9` unauthorized, `10` not found and `11` invalid, the class named at the start of the error line. A failure no call to the tracker caused still exits `1`. [do-item's tracker operations](plugin/skills/do-item/SKILL.md#tracker-operations) list them.
actions.instruction: A runbook or script that reads `tracker.ts`'s exit `1` as every failure reads `6` to `11` as failures too.

actions.description: **Codex: the turn-budget hook is registered by `jig upgrade`, not shipped by the plugin.** Codex re-reviews a plugin's hooks whenever any file of the plugin changes, and skips them until it is approved again. The Codex plugin now ships none. `jig upgrade` adds one `PreToolUse` entry to `$CODEX_HOME/hooks.json` (`~/.codex` by default) whose command never changes and runs the installed plugin copy's guard, so approving it once with `/hooks` stands across releases. After this release, approve the guard once in each Codex home; until then it does not run there. Run `jig upgrade --codex` with `CODEX_HOME` set to give another home the entry. `jig uninstall --machine --yes` removes it. Claude Code is unchanged.
actions.instruction: Run `jig upgrade --codex` and approve the guard with `/hooks` in every Codex home that runs unattended passes.

actions.description: **Breaking:** the dispatcher starts an assigned epic's ready children in parallel when the epic has no execution plan, up to a per-epic width, instead of one child at a time. The width is the new `dispatch.epic_width` key of the repository's `dispatch` section, read from the default branch, and defaults to 4. A started child counts toward it while it still needs an agent, and so does a child that cannot be read; a child in `ops_pending` or waiting on a person does not. A child that waits on the width names the epic and the width. A repository that wants the old behaviour sets `dispatch.epic_width: 1`. An epic with an execution plan is unchanged, and an interactive `do-item` session still takes one child. The audit's configuration schema gains the key. Why: [ADR-0024](docs/adr/ADR-0024-epic-children-are-admitted-in-parallel.md).
actions.instruction: A repository whose epics must run one child at a time sets `dispatch.epic_width: 1`; runbooks that say the dispatcher works an epic one child at a time say what is true now.

actions.description: Finished worktrees are no longer kept just for the `.fallow` tool cache. Repositories can declare other rebuildable ignored paths with `gc.regenerable_paths`; undeclared content remains protected. Existing installations refresh the collector after upgrading, even without configuration changes, to confirm new default bounds.
actions.instruction: After upgrading, review the preview and run `jig install gc --repo <repository> --yes` for every existing installation.

actions.description: **Breaking:** The shared configuration reader refuses a rule that names an unknown fact or gives a value of the wrong kind in any of these fields, naming the field and the file that set it, before any skill acts on it, and the audit reports it. A malformed rule a skill never read (such as a `do_item.gates` entry) used to be ignored; now every skill, `jig gc` and `jig dispatch` stop on it. A `do_item.gates` entry do-item refuses (no labels or paths, no skill, an unknown field, a glob that does not compile) now also stops `determine_agent.ts`, `determine_route.ts`, work-batch and the dispatcher's batch planning, where before nothing read the field. An empty key in `do_item.agents.labels`, `codearea_areas` or `title_keywords` is refused too (an empty title keyword used to match every title).
actions.instruction: Run the audit's configuration fit and fix each rule it refuses: `rejected:every skill (rule matcher)` and `rejected:do-item (review gates)`.

actions.description: **Breaking:** `work_batch.solo_flags`, and the solo-only flags work-batch derives, match an item's labels ignoring case, as every other label rule does: an issue labelled `Privacy-Review` is now held out of a batch by `solo_flags: [privacy-review]`, where before it was batched. The dispatcher's batch grouping reads the same rule.
actions.instruction: Check that no label you batch differs from a solo-only flag only in case; rename it if it should stay batchable.

actions.description: A route's reasons name the configuration rule that matched in the matcher's wording: `tier: complex (routing.complex_flags, for the item's label has-migration)` and `effort: high (raised from medium: routing.raise.flags, for the item's label has-migration)`, where they read `flag has-migration` before.
actions.instruction: Update a runbook or script that reads the old reason text.

actions.description: Deferred review findings enter the backlog in one open issue per pull request and issue type on every supported tracker. Later findings append to the same issue, with the highest priority and union of categories; native related links preserve the originating issue and epic without adding children to their scope.
actions.instruction: Replace runbook rules that parent deferred findings to an epic with backlog batches and related links. Existing follow-ups are not backfilled.

hints.value: Findings deferred while the epic is live still go to the epic

actions.description: **Breaking:** `do-item` and `drive-pr` no longer rename the Orca or Herdr workspace they run in as the work moves from implementing to driving to ready. A workspace keeps the name it was created with, or the one a person gives it; where the work stands shows on the Orca board card, the workspace's comment, the pull request and the dispatch dashboard. The `workspace_name` section (`template`, `statuses`) has no effect: a file that still sets it loads as before, and the audit's configuration check notes it once. The `workspace-name.ts` script is gone.
actions.instruction: Remove `workspace_name` from `.config/jig.yaml`, and any runbook step that expects a renamed workspace.

actions.description: **Breaking:** A rearm label without a stop-bound request expires.
actions.instruction: Replace steps that apply the rearm label directly with the rearm command in Jig Send. Re-send older pending requests that still need to run.

actions.description: **Breaking:** The dispatcher orders ready pickups by overlap with work in flight and how long each pickup has waited. A free slot can take overlapping work. The retired `dispatch.epic_width` key is ignored and the dispatch receipt points to `dispatch.overlap`.
actions.instruction: Remove `dispatch.epic_width` and update runbooks that use it. To require one child at a time, use execution plan dependency edges or a serialized area. Configure `dispatch.overlap` to tune shared-file admission.

actions.description: The [epic closure sweep](plugin/skills/do-item/README.md#the-epic-closure-sweep) proposes closure for delivered scope, identifies unfinished work for the backlog, and records a person's reply as the waiver. It checks the plan and moves outstanding checks before closing an accepted epic.
actions.instruction: To transfer person-only checks at epic closure, set `issue_tracker.person_checks` to the key of a standing open issue.

actions.description: On Linear, an issue assigned within three minutes of its creation was never started: Linear leaves changes made in an issue's first three minutes out of its history, so the dispatcher found no assignment and refused the item on every tick. `jig send … assign` now waits until that window has passed before writing, and for an item already assigned to the factory identity whose history shows no assignment it refuses with the remedy (unassign it, then send again) instead of the bare "already assigned". The served-queue documentation and the operator skill say the same.
actions.instruction: A runbook that assigns a Linear item to the factory identity or a served person right after filing it should wait three minutes, or unassign and assign it again after them.

actions.description: **Breaking:** The dispatcher no longer starts an item that has no priority, assigned or from the ready pool, which it used to place after every low-priority item. The line lists the item in its queue with the priority it lacks; once a person sets one, or the steward's `facet` record fills it for an assigned item, the next tick ranks and starts it. A repository that wants such items started anyway sets `dispatch.missing_priority: start` ([configuration](plugin/CONFIGURATION.md#dispatch)).
actions.instruction: Give the items the dispatcher starts a priority, or set `dispatch.missing_priority: start` where the repository does not rank its items.
